issues.problem: The map's arrows land on the wrong rows at both widths. The top map row 'K1 → 04' routes into row 03 ('K3 V3'), and 'K3 → 03' routes into row 04 ('K1 V1′'). This is the figure that introduces the in-memory map, so it shows the map pointing at the wrong entries while its own labels say otherwise. Fig 8·a and the append-only-log clip route the same arrows correctly.
issues.fix: Re-route both connectors so each ends on its labelled offset: K1 → row 04, K3 → row 03. Use the clip's routing (the K1 elbow goes down past the K3 elbow, nested so the lines don't cross), or swap the map rows so K3 is listed first, as in fig-8a. Check the desktop and the phone redraw.

issues.problem: The prose contradicts the 'More precisely' boxes and the figure next to it. The prose says 'Bitcask is used by Uber in production, for its main ride-hailing service… Uber uses Riak as its main database'. The box right below says Bitcask ran at Uber through Riak, 'but not as the store of the main ride-hailing data'. The prose then lists 'master-slave architecture, consensus' as what Riak adds. The next box and Fig 10·b say Riak is masterless ('no master: keys hashed onto a ring'). A reader gets two opposite claims within one screen.
issues.fix: Rewrite the two paragraphs so the prose agrees with the boxes. Say that Uber ran Riak, with Bitcask underneath, for parts of its dispatch services. Say that Riak adds partitioning onto a ring, replication to N nodes, request routing from any node and data movement, without a master. Then trim the boxes to the sources only, so they stop correcting the prose.

issues.problem: The page narrates the teacher instead of stating the ideas. This is lec01 critic #14 again. 'the instructor' appears 13 times and 'the class' 55 times. There is teacher biography in the body and in a figure. Examples: Fig 3·b's label 'the instructor's own database would start with AODB'. The aside title 'From the instructor: reload by deploying' and its 'For a couple of his own services…'. 'The instructor implemented Bitcask about five years ago… which is why he is sure'. 'came across Bitcask in a storage paper-reading course in college'. 'surprised the instructor'. 'If it isn't, the instructor doesn't believe the high-throughput claim'.
issues.fix: Keep the provenance in the meta lines and the 'Redrawn from the class board' captions. Rewrite the rest as plain claims. Examples: 'Your own format would start with its own magic bytes, e.g. AODB'. Retitle the aside 'Reload by deploying'. Replace the benchmark anecdote with 'Implement it and benchmark it against an in-memory store on HDD and SSD'. Make 'no append-only file? ask how it gets its throughput' the heuristic itself. Remove the his/he references.

issues.problem: Phone step-throughs reserve the height of the final step from step 1. In fig-4c step 1, there are about 400px of empty lifelines between the one drawn row ('path = s3://…') and Prev/Next plus the step text. The drawing and its sentence are a screen apart. This is lec01 #6 and lec09 C-03 again.
issues.fix: Apply the lec01 fix: on phone, crop the viewBox to the rows up to the current step, growing as the reader steps, or shorten the lifelines. Prev/Next and the step text should then sit directly under the row that just changed.

issues.problem: On desktop the clip stage is about 540px wide and sits left in the 920px figure column, with empty paper to its right. Its lettering renders at about 18–24px with a heavy marker stroke ('≈ 500 GB', 'Mixed for a while, never garbage', 'disk full: crash'). The static figures beside it letter at about 13–14px with a pencil stroke. Fig 6·d sits one screen below Clip 6·1 and looks drawn by a different hand. This is the same as lec05 C-05 and lec09 C-06.
issues.fix: Pin the clip scale to the figures. Render the landscape composition across the full sheet width (about 920px), or keep 540px and reduce the composition's lettering, so that labels land at 14–16px and the beat caption at about 16px. Match the stroke width to the static figures. Centre the stage if it stays narrower than the sheet.

issues.problem: The overview's 'Our storage so far' section is two paragraphs and five 'back in' chips with no drawing. lec01's overview opens its 'so far' section with a figure. lec07 C-09 and lec08 C-09 raised the same problem.
issues.fix: Add a small 'so far' figure between the two paragraphs. On the left, lec09's Redis: one hash table in memory, a ring of nodes, and the append-only file. On the right, lec03's key-value rows in MySQL with the magic-value delete. Use key glyphs, and dim them as in lec01's 'Medium so far'. Keep only the 2–3 most relevant chips under it.

issues.problem: The verdicts are question-specific and agree with the reveals, which is good. But on all 9 cards the right answer is the second button, and it is usually the longer, more qualified one (e.g. 'Cost: you pay for the same terabyte on every server', 'Append a new K2 entry with a special "deleted" value'). After two cards the position gives the answer away. This is the same as lec07 C-08 and lec09 C-09.
issues.fix: Put the right answer first on about half the cards (e.g. §3, §5, §7, §9). Balance option lengths so the wrong option is as specific as the right one, e.g. §4: 'Updates: a weekly push to 100 servers drifts out of sync'.

issues.problem: Two figures share the number 7·b ('Fig 7·b' and 'Fig 7·b, complete'). lec01 critic #8 fixed the same problem. The second figure repeats the first figure's file and command list, adding the delete and the map.
issues.fix: Number the second figure 7·c and shift the later ones (7·c → 7·d), or merge the two into one step-through: puts, then the delete, then the map.

issues.where: 6-switching-servers / fig-6a and its think card, fig/1440-light-fig-6a.png, fig/390-light-fig-6a.png, fig/1440-light-6-switching-servers-think1-after.png
issues.problem: The numbers disagree with the drawing. The index entry is 'apple: 100, 1024' and the step text says the read is 1,024 bytes long, but it 'returns apple, a fruit', a single 14-byte line. A 1,024-byte read would return dozens of lines. The rows also mix formats: 'aah, to exclaim' and 'bat, a club' have a space after the comma, while 'apple,a fruit' (and every earlier figure) has none.
issues.fix: Use a length that matches the line ('apple: 100, 14'), here and in the think card ('apple at offset 100, 14 bytes'). Write every row in the page's 'word,meaning' format with no space.

issues.problem: The static merge figure shows its final state: the new dictionary is complete and the changelog is marked 'done'. But both blue pointers still sit on 'c'. The caption says 'Blue marks the current pair of pointers', so the drawing shows a state that never happens. The clip poster gets this right, with the pointers past the end.
issues.fix: Move both pointers past the last entry, under the dashed end rows as in the clip poster. Or draw the figure mid-merge, at the c/c″ match with the output filled only to b.

issues.problem: K1's connector has an arrowhead into file 002, but K2's connector has none. It also takes a long detour under the files before it climbs into 003. The unlabeled arrow entering 003 from the right is the write path, but nothing names it, unlike 'writes go here' in Fig 8·a.
issues.fix: Add an arrowhead where K2's line enters 003, and route it above the files instead of around the bottom. Label the right-hand arrow 'writes go here' to match Fig 8·a.

issues.problem: The three API servers' reads merge onto one shared trunk before reaching S3, so you can't tell each server makes its own ranged read. This is the lec01 #11 pattern. Fig 4·b also has a stray leading pipe in '| hdfs · network hdd'.
issues.fix: Give each api its own connector into the cloud (three short parallel arrows, or a fan into three ports), and put '(file, off, n)' on one of them. Write 'hdfs · network hdd' without the pipe.

issues.problem: Fig 9·c's record starts with an empty, unlabelled cell before KSZ. The CRC slot is drawn before the CRC is introduced, and nothing says what it is. The paper rectangles behind the step annotations ('crash: the value is cut short', 'restart: scan from the top') render lighter than the sheet and extend past the text, so they show as pale patches over the grid.
issues.fix: Either drop the blank cell until step 4, or label it 'CRC?' in grey. Fill the label rectangles with the sheet's paper token and size them to the text plus about 4px.

issues.problem: The first knob is labelled '1. MC freq'. 'MC' is a board abbreviation that the page never expands, and the prose says 'merge and compaction'.
issues.fix: Write '1. merge & compaction frequency' (or 'merge frequency') in the figure and the clip.

issues.problem: The 'back in · Lecture N' chips sit flush under the last line of the paragraph, with no top margin. They read as part of the paragraph's last line, and on phone two stacked chips crowd the next paragraph. This is the same as lec07 C-21.
issues.fix: Give block-level cross-reference chips about 8px top margin and 12px bottom margin, the same as in the overview's chip list.

issues.problem: At 1024 the six-column comparison table squeezes each column to about 90px. Headers break to one word per line ('Switch / at a / known / time'), and a red cell ('Switches anyway, to a missing or…') runs down five lines.
issues.fix: Below about 1100px, transpose the table (options as rows, the four questions as columns), or let it scroll horizontally with the first column sticky.

issues.problem: The left rail marks Lecture 07, 'Instagram photos and hashtags', as 'coming soon' in grey, although lec07 is published. This may only be a QA build artifact (lec02 C-10).
